recommendations.verdict: 本周最硬的一篇取证长文：用链上数据把 EIP-7702 委派攻击拆到逐笔交易的粒度
recommendations.reason: 它不是在讲「交易所被黑了」，而是给出一个可复用的失效模型：签名有效 ≠ 签名生效，而「生效」的授权可以落在组织所有应急开关的射程之外。凡是做钱包、托管、签名服务或 agent 凭证的人都该读。

recommendations.full_analysis:
一句话判断：这是本周最值得花时间的一篇安全取证——它把「签名有效」和「签名生效」拆成两件独立的事，再用链上数据证明，一件生效的授权可以活得比组织的应急开关更久。

1. 攻击的形状。2026-10-29 20:20:59 UTC，区块 26,300,753 第 138 位的一笔 type-4 交易里塞了 50 个 EIP-7702 授权，nonce 覆盖 18,914,775 到 18,914,824，链 id 全是 1，全部指向同一个 1,674 字节的 sweeper 合约。50 个签名用 EIP-7702 的消息格式都能恢复出 Binance 14 这个热钱包——也就是说，它们全部是密码学意义上有效的。

2. 为什么只有一个生效。EIP-7702 执行时拿每个授权的 nonce 和签名者当下的 nonce 比对，不等就跳过，跳过不影响列表继续往下走，而签名消息里根本没有时间字段。交易执行时 Binance 14 的 nonce 正好是 18,914,809，于是那一个匹配、nonce 加一、账户代码从空变成 0xef0100 加上 sweeper 地址。更巧的是：同区块第 133 位，Binance 14 自己发了一笔经「钱包 34」转出 5 USDC 的普通交易，把 nonce 推到 18,914,809。没有这 5 USDC，生效的会是 18,914,808 那个授权，装的是同一份代码——换张票，同一结果。

3. 3 小时 49 分里发生了什么。首次扫掠在 20:24:23（委派后 3 分 24 秒），取走 167,464.2479 ETH 和 63 笔代币转账（含 1,615,409,498.97 USDT）。之后 6 次调用继续取，5 次扫 Binance 14 合计 172,624.4046 ETH，每次恰好留 1 ETH；关联钱包 34 被取走 823,000,000 USDC，靠的是 Binance 14 本来就有的调用权限（selector 0x043ff9d2）。最刺眼的一段是补血：半小时一次的归集任务和一笔 200,000,000 USDT 的储备补款一直在往这个已被控制的钱包里打钱，后者到账 72 秒就被扫走。Tether 在首扫后 37 分 12 秒冻结收款地址时，已有 7 亿 USDT 转出。直到 00:10:35 币安自己发了一笔指向零地址的 type-4 交易，委派才被清掉。

recommendations.title: 端到端 4-bit 训练：把 NVFP4 前向放进生产训练配方
recommendations.verdict: 低精度训练从论文配方走到生产运行的完整工程记录，取舍写得比结论更有价值
recommendations.reason: 文章没有停在「我们省了内存」，而是把每个阶段的误差敏感度分开算：前向用 4-bit、反向用 8-bit、通信再单独量化，最后给出 2% 计算效率损失换来的墙钟收益。这是少见的、能照着抄的训练栈细节。
key_points: NVFP4 每值 4.5 bit、GB300 上 15 PFLOPS，相比 BF16 的 16 bit / 2.5 PFLOPS，位宽少 3.6 倍、吞吐高 6 倍
前向用 NVFP4 + 专用 kernel，反向退到 MXFP8 并引入随机舍入：因为 block scaling 一转置，1×16 的块就错位，用 16×16 tile 又太粗
加速后新瓶颈是专家并行的通信：NVLink 900 GB/s 对 15 PFLOPS，等于每收到 1 字节要配 16,000 次浮点运算，于是 combine 改用 32 维随机 Hadamard 变换 + S2F6，把 16 bit 压到 8.25 bit
较大训练任务实测：预训练墙钟快 8%、RL 快 20%，预训练计算效率代价约 2%；Inkling 2 Small 在 GB300 NVL72 上 68 小时完成预训练
recommendations.full_analysis:
一句话判断：这是把「端到端 4-bit 训练」从论文配方推到生产运行的一份工程记录，价值在于它写清了每一步为什么这么选，而不是只报一个加速比。

1. 起点是一个简单算术。NVFP4 每值 4.5 bit（(4×16+8)÷16），在 GB300 上是 15 PFLOPS；MXFP8 是 8.25 bit / 5 PFLOPS；BF16 是 16 bit / 2.5 PFLOPS。位宽少 3.6 倍，吞吐高 6 倍——这个缺口足够大到值得忍受量化误差。但作者一开始直接全 NVFP4 训练，计算效率（CE）掉得无法接受，于是改为按阶段拆：前向最能容忍误差、反向最不能容忍偏差（bias）。

2. 真正的卡点不是精度，是转置。前向里 NVFP4 按 1×16 的块算 scale，反向要把张量转置，块就变成按列取 16 个值，分组全变、scale 全变，大量值直接被舍成零。NVIDIA 的解法是用 16×16 的 tile 算单一 scale，转置前后一致；作者试过，太粗，CE 还是不可接受。他们的做法是：把前向张量反量化到高精度、转置、再用随机舍入重新量化到 MXFP8。随机舍入按距离概率上取或下取，保证期望值不变——只需要前向反向张量「在期望上相等」，不需要逐位相等。这一步是整个配方的支点。

3. 加速之后瓶颈换了位置。MoE 的前向 GEMM 理论上快了三倍，结果卡在专家并行的通信上：在 GB300 NVL72 上 NVLink 每向 900 GB/s，而 NVFP4 GEMM 能跑 15 PFLOPS，折算下来每收到 1 字节就得配 16,000 次浮点运算，否则 Tensor Core 就在空等。dispatch 阶段直接传 NVFP4 就够了；combine 阶段输出必须保持较高精度，他们先试 MXFP8，被离群值坑了，最后用 32 维随机 Hadamard 变换把数据「转平滑」，再量化到 block-scaled S2F6（2 位整数 + 6 位小数），把传输量从 16 bit 压到 8.25 bit，精度无损。

4. 配方细节与代价。最后 16.6% 的层留在 MXFP8（NVIDIA 的配方是 15%，他们按 6 倍层数阶梯取 1/6）；激活量化用 Four Over Six 在两个 scale 之间选，权重不用；权重按专家、激活按 token 取外层 scale，借了 Composer 2 的做法。代价写得很直白：预训练 CE 损失约 2%，换 NVFP4 的速度；最大规模任务上预训练墙钟快 8%、RL 快 20%，RL 的 reward 无可测差异。Inkling 2 Small 是他们所知最大的、前向原生 4-bit 端到端训练模型，68 小时预训练完成。

5. 值得记住的两句。一是「十六年前没人相信能用少于 32 bit 训练」，今天 BF16 已经被称为高精度；二是他们的 BBBK kernel 同时压满 NVLink、ALU 和 Tensor Core——低精度训练的瓶颈往往是 ALU 侧的 scale 计算、随机舍入、数据合并，而不是矩阵乘本身。

我的推荐：如果你在做训练或推理的成本优化，第 2、3 节（转置错配、随机舍入、通信量化）是可以直接搬的工程结论；如果只是想知道趋势，记住一句话就够：4-bit 不是推理的专利，它已经在预训练配方里，代价被量化成 2% 的计算效率。

recommendations.title: AI 写代码的时代，怎么把 CI 提速
recommendations.verdict: 把「agent 提交速度 > CI 检查速度」这个新瓶颈讲清楚的一份可执行清单
recommendations.reason: 五个动作都有具体做法和踩坑点（缓存 key 别带时间戳、必需检查不能用 path filter、部署流水线不要用 cancel-in-progress），适合直接对照自家 workflow 改。
key_points: 瓶颈有了数字：GitHub 一周 2.75 亿次提交、全年奔 140 亿（2025 年约 10 亿），Actions 一周 21 亿分钟（2023 年 5 亿）
缓存要用 lockfile 哈希做 key 并配 restore-keys，key 里带时间戳或 commit SHA 等于永远不命中；Dockerfile 先装依赖再拷源码
分片有上限：每个 shard 都要付自己的启动成本，超过临界点只加钱不加速度；`fail-fast: false` 让所有分片跑完一次看全失败
少做无用功最便宜：path filter 别用在必需检查上（会卡成 pending），monorepo 用 affected-only 要 checkout 足够历史，部署流水线禁用 cancel-in-progress
recommendations.full_analysis:
一句话判断：它把「agent 写码比 CI 检查快」这件事从体感变成了数字，然后给出五条按性价比排序的动作。

1. 先给瓶颈定量。2026 年 4 月 GitHub COO Kyle Daigle 说平台一周处理 2.75 亿次提交、按年化 140 亿（2025 年约 10 亿）；同一周 GitHub Actions 跑了 21 亿分钟，2023 年是 5 亿。也就是说 agent 的产出全部堆进了 CI：15 分钟的流水线，一个人一天推几次还能忍，一个 agent 一下午开十个 PR，它就变成了队列。

2. 先测量，别猜。多数团队对最慢步骤的判断是错的——感觉是测试慢，实际可能是 90 秒装依赖 + 30 秒跑测试。做法很朴素：看最近十次运行的逐步耗时，取中位数而不是最差值，并把排队时间、环境准备时间、执行时间分开看，因为三者的解法完全不同。

3. 缓存与分层。actions/cache 的关键全在 key：用 lockfile 哈希，依赖不变 key 就不变；restore-keys 是常被漏掉的一半——精确 key 不命中时能退到较旧的缓存，只补装新增的包。反过来，key 里塞时间戳或 commit SHA 就是永不命中、每次都存一份新缓存。Docker 同理：先拷 lockfile 装依赖、再拷源码，代码改动就不会重建安装层；跨运行复用层用 BuildKit 的 type=gha 后端。

4. 硬件与并行。私有仓库默认 runner 只有 2 vCPU / 7 GB，这是很多「CI 慢」的真实原因。作者引用的第三方基准（RunsOn 的公开测试，关掉缓存，Rust 测试 + TypeScript 类型检查 + PostHog 生产 Docker 构建）里，4 vCPU 档的 Avrea 约 7 分钟对 GitHub 4 核 runner 约 18.5 分钟。分片则要认清边际收益：四个 shard 能把 12 分钟压到 3 分钟，但每个 shard 都要付一遍启动成本，超过临界点只增加花费；少数特别重的文件要单独拆，否则会有一个 shard 拖尾。

5. 最便宜的一条：少跑。path filter 能把文档改动挡在全量构建之外，但必需检查不能用它——检查永远不跑，PR 会卡在 pending，正确做法是让 workflow 跑起来、用 if 条件跳掉 job（跳过的 job 算通过）。monorepo 用 Nx/Turborepo/Bazel 的 affected 只测受影响的包，注意 checkout 默认只取一个 commit，比较 main 需要足够历史。最后，连续两次推送时先跑的那次已经过期，用 concurrency 组取消；但部署流水线不要这么做，中途取消会留下坏状态，应该排队。

我的推荐：照着做第一、五条就能拿到大部分收益——先量出真正最慢的三步，再砍掉不必跑的工作。它引用的 runner 数据来自厂商自己的基准（作者也标了 Avrea 是文中的服务商），选型时用自家 workflow 复测一遍比看榜单可靠。

items.title: The avalanche that hit math is coming for AI development (50 minute read)
items.summary: AI's capabilities in mathematics exploded quickly. Current AIs can now complete well-scoped problems in mathematics easily. This ability to solve well-scoped problems is going to be an even bigger deal for machine learning research than for mathematics. AI labs mainly care about how any new algorithmic recipe empirically makes training more efficient or elicits smarter models - they don't care about theory for its own sake.
items.score_reason: 数学能力跃迁对 ML 研发方式的冲击，长文论证
items.highlight: Dwarkesh 引用 METR 称 Anthropic 研发速度一年翻倍、Claude 已主导其 26% 的 AI 研发，并以数学爆发为预演，中位预期 2028 年追平顶尖研究员。
items.excerpt: If you asked me earlier this year how far away we are from superintelligence, I’d probably have said at least the better part of a decade. But over the last three months, I’ve updated my views a ton. I’ve been debating people about this question, both on and off the podcast.

items.summary: Meta researchers explored which components of vision encoders are essential for multimodal models, finding that dedicated visual processing capacity matters more than pretraining.

items.summary: Physicist Nathaniel Craig worked with GPT-6 Astra to develop a candidate lattice formulation of the Standard Model, addressing a longstanding challenge in defining the theory without relying on perturbative approximations. Astra helped construct the mathematical framework and develop a detailed proof supporting the proposed approach.

items.summary: Anthropic emphasizes the importance of robust safety evaluations for AI models, which inform deployment and training decisions.

items.title: Cyber Chaos Monkey: Staying Ahead of Security Threats With AI Agents (7 minute read)
items.summary: Shopify's Cyber Chaos Monkey is an agentic vulnerability hunter that attacks its live production systems using test credentials, source code, and past bug reports. It sends probes, reads the production logs, and checks the results against source code to refine each exploit. Shopify said tens of thousands of runs have turned up dozens of serious findings without an outage. Containment relies on read-only ephemeral credentials, a credential-swapping proxy, an egress allowlist, plus a separate "judge" agent running a different model that watches the attacker agent live and ends the run if it breaks the rules of engagement or stops responding.
items.score_reason: Shopify 用 agent 主动攻击生产系统的实践
items.highlight: Shopify 的 Cyber Chaos Monkey 让 agent 持临时生产凭据在 k8s pod 内自主攻击真实系统，由异模型裁判实时读取执行日志、违规即杀，已跑数万次演练、发现数十个有效问题且无事故。
items.excerpt: We're obsessed with protecting merchant and buyer data. We reinvent our security programs relentlessly, throwing away what doesn't keep pace with the evolving landscape and challenging ourselves to multiply both the depth and coverage of our capabilities with AI.

items.title: Making a programming language (7 minute read)
items.summary: A compiler is a line of small programs. Each turns one shape into the next. The programs transform text into tokens and tokens into a tree, then the tree gets checked, and either an interpreter runs it or it becomes a native binary. No single stage is hard - the work is in making errors useful and keeping two backends in agreement.
items.score_reason: 从词法到解释器手写编程语言的教学长文
items.highlight: 作者自建语言：200 行词法、约 2300 行类型检查器、Perceus 式引用计数，1080 个测试双后端对拍并跑 sanitizer，解释器 fib(32) 从 1.57s 降到 0.36s。
items.excerpt: I'm making a programming language. Naming is hard, so until it has a name it's ████ here, and `obfuscated` in commands. I wanted a program to compile down to what it actually needs and nothing more, and to be secure by default, not after an audit.

items.title: AI, work from home, and the young-graduate job market (15 minute read)
items.summary: New college graduates are employed less than a few years ago. While AI may be a factor, there's growing evidence that work from home is an important factor moving the needle on young-graduate employment. AI exposure and teleworkability are highly correlated with each other, making it hard to distinguish definitively between the two factors. The full extent of AI's effects on the labor market might not manifest until the next recession.
items.score_reason: 用数据拆解应届生就业与远程办公、AI 暴露度的关系
items.highlight: 基于 CPS 的回归显示，远程办公普及度可解释 2023 年以来应届生就业率下滑的 56%–88%，AI 暴露度在控制 WFH 后不显著，Stripe 支付数据同向，但作者自认并非因果。
items.excerpt: Young college graduates in the US are seeing a weakening labor market. Among workers age 22–26 holding a bachelor's degree, their employment-population ratio was 88% in September 2026, a full percentage point below where it was three years earlier.

items.summary: Marathon Fusion, a San Francisco-based fusion startup, claims it has created gold from mercury. The startup has not published how much gold it made, and the process requires a fusion plant that does not exist yet. Many fields currently rely on isotopes from aging reactors. Marathon Fusion's process could unlock a world of abundant isotopes, opening up many markets and possibilities.

items.title: Building always-on agents (14 minute read)
items.summary: Always-on agents run indefinitely, managing context across sessions and taking action without direct supervision. They have surged in popularity lately, largely due to recent model advancements that have made them more practical to run. Models now have better judgment and are more reliable, and intelligence is becoming cheaper. This post breaks down the primitives behind always-on agents and walks through how they fit together.

items.excerpt: Over the past few months, we’ve seen a resurgence of always-on agents. Always-on agents are stateful and proactive, meaning they manage context across sessions and take actions without direct supervision. Underneath, they run on the same core loop as other agents.

items.summary: This post disentangles the three components involved in recursive self-improvement and shows how the deep learning paradigm forces researchers to consider what counts as the 'self' undergoing improvement.

items.title: Quark: our whole training stack, end to end, for $4,200 (7 minute read)
items.summary: Quark is a language model with about 165 million parameters trained for about $4,200 of compute (about 1,300 H-100-hours). It has the best benchmark average among open models of its size trained on similar token budgets. The model was created to explore every part of the training stack the team was using before spending serious money on a large model. This post looks at the model's data, architecture, pretraining at scale, context extension, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and release.
items.score_reason: 165M 参数模型从零训练全栈的成本与配方公开
items.highlight: Empero 用约 1300 H100 小时（约 4200 美元）走完 165M 模型全流程：500B token 预训练、128K 上下文扩展、纯 GRPO 强化学习，四个权重以 Apache-2.0 开源。
items.excerpt: Before we scale up, we wanted proof that every part of our stack works. Quark is that proof: a 165M-parameter model with 128K context that we took from raw data through pretraining, long-context training, reinforcement learning, evaluation and release for about $4,200 of compute.

items.title: On the Brutality of Amdahl's Law (12 minute read)
items.summary: The world is far too slow to see the high double-digit or more economic growth and seismic transformations in the economy that AI is predicted to bring. Intelligence isn't the only technology curve to go quasi-infinite in the last century and a half. Electricity, communication, computers, transportation, and agriculture have all experienced extreme growth and transformation. Despite this, we've only seen 2% GDP per capita growth for nearly 150 years.
items.score_reason: 用 Amdahl 定律约束 AI 经济影响预期的论证
items.highlight: 作者用 Amdahl 定律类比：即便智能无限快，物理制程、供应链、实验噪声与监管仍是瓶颈，分层瓶颈下整体只会得到常数倍提速，爆炸式增长难以成立，世界其实很慢。
items.excerpt: When I worked in theoretical physics research, I was constantly reminded that if I were just that much smarter and had read that many more papers, I would be able to make the right connection to solve the problem. You are always the bottleneck; it’s always a skill issue.

items.title: AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets (4 minute read)
items.summary: Arctic Wolf linked AntiFox, an open-source autonomous pentesting platform, to intrusions that deployed ASPX web shells through compromised IIS applications. Attackers extracted configuration data, database credentials, and AWS credentials, then used valid IAM identities to enumerate AWS services. Some activity reached production Secrets Manager values and S3 objects. AWS said its services were not compromised. It recommends least privilege, IMDSv2, removing long-term keys from application configurations, and GuardDuty.
items.score_reason: 开源自主渗透平台被用于真实入侵并取 AWS 凭据

items.excerpt: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a campaign in which an emerging agentic penetration testing platform called AntiFox has been used to steal Amazon Web Services (AWS) credentials and pivot laterally into compromised environments.

items.title: Policy and Disclosure: 2026 Edition (6 minute read)
items.summary: Google Project Zero has dropped its "90 + 30" disclosure policy for a "Full X" model. Bugs are now disclosed a fixed number of days after they are reported, whether or not they have been fixed. The window starts at 90 days, moves to 60 on February 2, 2027, and to 30 on January 3, 2028, and grace periods and variant rules are gone. The team said LLMs have made exploits from patches almost instantaneous, which makes post-patch soak time pointless, and have raised its bug volume to several per week in targets that used to yield a few a year.
items.score_reason: Project Zero 放弃 90+30 改为固定期限披露
items.highlight: Project Zero 改用 Full X 政策：即日起报告后 90 天公开，2027 年 2 月转 60 天、2028 年 1 月转 30 天，删除宽限期与变体例外，也不再以是否修复作为公开条件。
items.excerpt: Since 2021, Project Zero has followed a “90 + 30” vulnerability disclosure policy, allowing vendors up to 90 days to remediate a vulnerability plus an extra 30 days “soak time” for patch rollout.

items.title: Post-Quantum Authentication: Lessons from Prague (11 minute read)
items.summary: At an October IAB workshop in Prague, users deploying post-quantum authentication reported no security problems with ML-DSA or SLH-DSA, but said signature size kept breaking old limits. An ML-DSA-65 signature is 3,309 bytes compared with 64 for Ed25519, which pushes handshakes past congestion windows, signed requests past URL limits, and firmware past device memory. The co-chairs argued that a migration is not finished until verifiers stop accepting classical roots, something Cisco expects some router certificates will not do until around 2035, and they also flagged AI coding agents as a new source of divergence because agents hand-roll incompatible crypto formats instead of calling libraries.
items.score_reason: 后量子签名部署真实踩坑：签名体积撞旧上限
items.highlight: IAB 布拉格工作坊结论：ML-DSA 签名 3309 字节对 Ed25519 的 64 字节，撑爆握手与 URL 限额；验证方更新最慢却须先迁移，且删掉经典根才算迁移完成。

items.title: The Binance Heist, Part One: Fifty Valid Signatures, One That Landed, and an Authority That Stood for 3 Hours 49 Minutes (38 minute read)
items.summary: On October 29, an attacker sent a single Ethereum transaction to Binance's "Binance 14" hot wallet carrying 50 EIP-7702 authorizations, all validly signed by the wallet's key. The one matching the wallet's current nonce took effect, so the wallet ran the attacker's sweeper contract as its own code for 3 hours 49 minutes and was drained seven times while automated top-ups kept refilling it. Binance's withdrawal suspension could not touch the delegation, which acted on-chain outside its withdrawal systems, and how the attacker reached Binance's internal signing service has not been explained beyond Binance's own account, so custody teams should monitor hot wallets for code appearing and keep a pre-built EIP-7702 revocation procedure ready.
